source: the game manual, read rather than recalled: Contra (Re-Translation).pdf in archive.org/details/rx2MRPnes1250pxPDF — the Japanese Famicom manual, which is the one matching this ROM. See docs/manuals.md. Entries below name the page they come from.
notes: The wall at the end of the jungle is destroyed by its cannons and the sensor between them; point-blank diagonal fire is what reaches them.
A base stage does not scroll. Its exit opens when the room's sensor is destroyed, and the way on is upward through the door.
Flying capsules carry weapons; shooting one and walking into what it drops is worth a detour.
Once a room's sensor is destroyed the way on is upward through the door, so a cleared room rewards moving up the screen.
The door out of a base room is in the middle of the far wall, near screen x=112; walking up anywhere else does nothing.

facts.statement: Press START to begin play from the title screen.

citation.figure: title screen prompt; page not yet pinned in the scan

facts.statement: The title offers a 1 PLAYER / 2 PLAYER choice; START or A confirms.

citation.figure: player-select screen; page not yet pinned in the scan

facts.statement: The gun fires in eight directions, including left and up-left 45°, not only rightward.

citation.quote: 左に発砲 / 左斜め上45°に発砲 in the control table

facts.statement: Firing left is a printed control, so mirrored templates are in the game and not a symmetry invented by the candidate set.
On 3D screens the gun points forward only: UP advances, LEFT and RIGHT strafe, DOWN goes prone. The base sensor is reached by stepping sideways until the shot lines up, not by aiming left.

scope.why: the manual scopes this to 3D screens

citation.quote: 3D画面では前方にのみ攻撃発砲します

facts.statement: Scroll is vertical, horizontal or 3D depending on the area; underwater is a further mode of its own (no jumping, no firing downward). The prior's scope should follow this axis.

citation.quote: AREAによって画面のスクロールが縦、横、3Dと切り替わります

facts.statement: Destroying the zone's detection sensor is the advance condition. Base 1 is a maze of sensors around an evil core at its centre.

citation.quote: US manual text: detection sensor is the advance condition in every zone

facts.statement: Once the room's sensor is destroyed the way on is upward through the door in the middle of the far wall.

citation.figure: route note; the door's central position is from the base-room picture, page not yet pinned in the scan

facts.statement: Flying capsules carry weapons; shooting one and walking into what it drops is worth a detour.

citation.figure: power-up / capsule figure; page not yet pinned in the scan

facts.statement: A cleared stage grants an extra life. The death price does not currently know this.

citation.quote: US manual: cleared stage grants an extra life

facts.statement: B button: fire left or right (左又は右に発砲).
B + down + left: fire lower-left 45° (左斜め下45°に発砲).
B + left: fire left (左に発砲).
B + up + left: fire upper-left 45° (左斜め上45°に発砲).
B alone or with pad: fire right or left (右又は左に発砲).
Firing covers eight directions: left, right, up-left 45°, down-left 45°, and the mirrored pair.
Pad down: lie prone (伏せる). A: climb down (下に降りる) or jump.

goal.statement: Destroy the zone's detection sensor to open the way on; in a base, work through the sensor maze toward the core.

notes: On 3D screens the gun points forward only.
Underwater: no jumping, no firing downward.

citations.quote: 3D画面では前方にのみ攻撃発砲します

realisation.types_why: object_tables.py scan: type 20 is the room sensor (base), 17/16/4 the jungle wall and cannon family. The manual only names sensor/wall/capsule; these numbers are the scan's answer to those words.
realisation.target_px_why: scrolling stages: wall 72 HP, destroying it ends the stage, worth ~928 px of the 4000 stride; 928/72 = 13 px per hit point.
realisation.found_by: object_tables.py / WALL_HP0 scan; recorded in docs/experiments.md A5

exit.way_on: upward through the door in the middle of the far wall
exit.statement: In a base room the exit opens when the sensor dies and is up; the door sits near the centre of the far wall.

realisation.found_by: manuals.md (door near screen x=112) + prior_exit_value in oracle_mpc.py; x=112 is from watching, not from RAM

economy.statement: A cleared stage grants an extra life.

citation.quote: 上 advances on 3D; upward is the way on in a base

scope.why: the base: byte 48 is the stage counter and 1 is the base. The manual says these things about a base stage — it does not scroll, its exit opens when the sensor dies, and the way on is upward. Applied to the jungle they tell the planner to climb and stand firing.
scope.target_px_why: the base: a room sensor is 8 hit points and destroying it opens the room, worth 667 px by the stage arithmetic (4000 over the six rooms measured 15 September). 667/8 = 83 px per hit point.
scope.target_types_why: the base: the manual says Base 1 is a maze where you destroy sensors and avoid the Royal Guard, so only the sensor is a target here. The rooms do carry wall-typed objects — 44 hit points of type 17 in room 3, 22 in rooms 1 and 4 — and counting those as targets priced a room at several times what it is worth.

target_px_why: scrolling stages: the wall at the end of a zone is 72 hit points (WALL_HP0, from the scan) and destroying it ends the stage, which is worth the distance left to the 4000 stride — about 928 px from the wall at 3072. 928/72 = 13 px per hit point. The old 40 was picked by hand and swamped progress: a whole screen is 256 px.
